elements.evidence: "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term."
"sole and exclusive provider" replaced with "a non-exclusive provider"

elements.element: No indirect purchase commitment or requirements obligation on Customer
elements.evidence: "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies"; "its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall" (untouched)

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: No exclusivity remains after redline: "a non-exclusive provider" — condition demonstrably absent
No exclusivity obligation exists to limit; "non-exclusive provider ... throughout the term"

elements.element: Automatic end of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: No exclusivity to terminate; obligation removed entirely in 2.2

reasons: The single replacement in 2.2 converts the sole-and-exclusive designation into a non-exclusive one, fully achieving the locked preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer).
Fallback limits (category, 12 months, automatic end on SLA/delivery failure) are vacuously satisfied because the exclusivity obligation itself no longer exists.
Change is minimal: a short phrase swap within one sentence; Section 2.1's no-commitment language and all other terms are untouched and remain effective.
No undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics are introduced; 'non-exclusive provider ... throughout the term' reads coherently.
The fallback offer appears only in the non-operative margin comment, which is appropriate and does not affect operative text.
